items.title: Inside the Secretive World of Campaign Ads Funded by AI Super PACs
items.excerpt: Bellingcat analysed more than 300 online video ad campaigns in the US midterms and traced ads backing candidates of both parties to the same AI-industry super PAC network, Leading the Future, which opposes AI rules that 'constrain' innovation and is funded by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and a16z.

items.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
items.excerpt: The New York Times and other publishers, including the New York Daily News and Chicago Tribune, filed lawsuits against Brave Software alleging unlawful scraping of their content to train and power AI and letting users bypass paywalls.

items.title: OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
items.excerpt: OpenAI announced a 'Grid Protectors Program', claiming on-site power for its AI campuses can lower electricity costs for other ratepayers, as public opposition to data centers becomes an election-season issue.

items.title: Prop 45 in California could be hiding a loophole for data centers
items.excerpt: California's Prop 45 on the Nov. 3 ballot could, critics say, open a path for AI data centers and energy projects to bypass local review, cutting communities out of siting decisions.

items.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
items.excerpt: WIRED uncovered some 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that look like regular AI tools but carry hidden features for creating violent and sexually abusive AI-generated images and video, raising app-store and deepfake-law enforcement questions.

items.title: Berlin unveils blueprint to catch up on AI
items.excerpt: A report from Germany's government AI task force, presented to the National Security Council, says Germany should become a 'sovereign AI nation' by 2030, securing access to leading models while building European alternatives with France and Canada.

items.title: India floats AI plan under which 'The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model'
items.excerpt: India's government proposed an AI architecture in which models are deployed to sit next to government and sectoral data rather than data being exported to Big Tech, aiming for more local AI without open access to national datasets.

items.title: China's AI Data Centers Move West, But Their Tax Revenue Stays East
items.excerpt: Under China's 'East Data, West Computing' push, AI data centers are clustering in western cities like Ulanqab, but tax revenue is booked in eastern headquarters, leaving host regions struggling to turn the compute boom into development.

items.title: Behind the Curtain: OpenAI's post-election power play
items.excerpt: Axios reports OpenAI plans a post-midterm policy and PR push, including rebranding data centers as 'AI compute campuses', as AI companies prepare for a changed Washington; OpenAI's Chris Lehane calls the election an 'electoral portal'.

items.title: Startups recalibrate Chinese AI for the West
items.excerpt: A growing number of startups are editing powerful Chinese open-weight models to strip censorship and security concerns for Western businesses, a workaround in the US-China AI competition.

items.title: Europe and Canada Plot a Digital Alliance as US Ties Fray
items.excerpt: After the EU-Canada summit agreement signed Oct. 30, Brussels and Ottawa announced expanded cooperation on digital trade, AI and tech infrastructure as tensions with the US deepen.

items.title: How AI Companies Want to Be Governed, and What That Means for AI Governance
items.excerpt: An analysis of recent public-governance pronouncements from Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI and what they imply for how AI will be regulated. (Analysis piece.)

items.title: There is No Universal Election Integrity Playbook for Platforms
items.excerpt: Op-ed arguing election integrity in the AI era is a product design problem as well as a content policy one, published on the eve of the US midterms. (Opinion piece.)

items.title: 정부는 AIDC 규제 완화 추진하는데…국회선 인허가 강화 움직임
items.excerpt: AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 특별법 시행을 앞두고 정부는 AIDC 인정 기준 완화에 나섰지만, 국회에서는 주민 안전과 생활환경 보호를 위한 인허가 규제 강화 법안이 잇따라 발의되고 있다.

items.title: 李대통령 "반도체·피지컬AI·AIDC에 21.3조...올해보다 두배"
items.excerpt: 이재명 대통령이 2일 국회 2027년도 예산안 시정연설에서 3대 메가프로젝트인 반도체·피지컬AI·AI 데이터센터에 올해의 두 배인 21.3조원을 투입하겠다고 밝혔다.

items.title: Faster planning decisions as new rules and AI tackle delays
items.excerpt: UK government release: from Oct. 31 a National Scheme of Delegation lets planning officers decide straightforward applications, alongside government-backed AI tools for councils to cut planning delays.

items.title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
items.excerpt: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters on Election Day. (Off-list: no on-list outlet carried an election-day chatbot piece.)

items.title: Exclusive: Election 'war rooms' enter the AI age
items.excerpt: Both OpenAI and Anthropic will run election 'war rooms' for the midterms, a first for both, to keep their platforms giving accurate voting information amid deepfake and AI-search misinformation threats. (Off-list; OpenAI's operations center was first reported Oct. 28 - the Anthropic war room is the new element.)

items.title: Voting in 2026 Is Getting an AI Slop 'I Voted' Sticker
items.excerpt: A polling place handed midterm voters 'I Voted' stickers bearing AI-generated artwork, a small sign of generative AI seeping into official election materials. (Off-list; light item.)
